identity.human_name: Recommend a human interface for a declared capability

purpose.plain_explanation: Validates declared capabilities and runtime context, ranks only eligible reusable interface patterns, plans beginner/advanced exposure, and emits separate receipts, assurance, health, and signal evidence without changing the source capability or shared contract.
purpose.why_it_matters: It exposes only the power needed for the goal while preserving source truth, safety gates, user choice, and recoverability.

Distinguish passed, failed, blocked, and untested handoffs
Refuse recommendation execution until the paired contract identity is accepted

Keep intake portable and bounded without executing producer code

Inspect stable anchor ZIP paths and inventory safely

Verify canonicalization vectors without importing producer code

required_inputs: context with goal, task, skill, device, resources, and collaboration mode
optional_inputs: Module One stable handoff anchor ZIP
input_constraints: Source capability facts must not be invented
Strict provenance requires a supplied source payload whose canonical SHA-256 matches the declaration
Paired intake requires exact accepted shared-contract identity and serialization
External anchor code is not imported or executed by the independent verifier
Context budget values must use declared module enums
Duplicate JSON object keys and non-finite JSON numbers are rejected
Explicit unsafe patterns and offline requirements are non-negotiable eligibility constraints
Anchor ZIPs must satisfy path and resource-consumption limits

expected_outputs: Selected reusable pattern or explicit blocked status
PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT_RUN for each handoff record
Ranked score trace with reasons and penalties
PASS or BLOCKED stable-anchor decision before record consumption
Exact schema hash and evidence-token conflict evidence
Recommendation execution state RUN or NOT_RUN
Bounded robustness classification with explicit synthetic-context limits
Signal-only packet for blocked or failed intake evidence
Signal-only packet for synthetic sensitivity and coverage observations
Decision drift causes based on changed receipt fingerprints
Advisory implementation-readiness checks that cannot grant execution authority
Hard eligibility blockers separate from score reasons and penalties
Explicit confirmation and non-destructive preview controls when declared by capability risk requirements
output_constraints: Recommendation does not modify the source capability
Confidence is not a success probability
Assurance does not alter the authoritative recommendation
Registry fingerprints identify the exact immutable registry snapshot used

failure_modes: Poor metadata can produce a blocked or weak recommendation
Registry weights may need domain calibration
A declared-only fixture hash cannot satisfy strict provenance without source payload bytes
A PASS result verifies contract/recommendation consistency, not underlying capability success
A producer may claim the same contract version while using different schema bytes
A semantic token adapter could conceal an unresolved contract fork if applied silently
A recommendation can be structurally valid while its implementation still needs assurance review
Unsupported accessibility needs require human review rather than invented deterministic handling
Overly permissive archive intake could exhaust resources if configured limits are bypassed

known_limitations: No learned model or empirical user-study calibration
Does not integrate into the local AXM runtime by itself
Fixture-surrogate PASS results do not prove cross-repository integration
The supplied stable anchor contains fixture evidence but not full Atlas Capability Records
The current paired merge is blocked by an unresolved shared-contract identity conflict
No real AXM registry intake was executed
Decision receipts prove deterministic input/output identity, not real-world interface usability
Evolution observations are advisory signals and do not prove that an architecture change is required
Synthetic robustness probes are bounded counterfactuals, not observed user behavior
Pattern coverage from one fixture batch cannot establish that unused patterns are unnecessary
The signal ledger is an integrity preview only and is not persisted into local AXM by this package
Recommendation Assurance uses transparent interaction-cost proxies for time and complexity rather than empirical user-study measurements
Accessibility coverage is rule-based and requires manual review for undeclared needs
Archive resource limits may require explicit revision for a legitimately larger future anchor

common_mistakes: Treating a recommendation as proof of capability
Treating equal version strings as proof of equal schema identity
Silently translating evidence-state tokens across contract forks
Treating synthetic counterfactual output as observed user evidence
Treating a blocked record retained as signal as an accepted executable record
Treating unused patterns in one batch as proof they should be removed
Treating a high score as permission to override an explicit hard constraint
Treating assurance REVIEW as an automatic rejection or as execution approval

accessibility_considerations: Machine-readable outputs can be rendered by alternate accessible front ends

beginner_layer_constraints: Do not expose execution controls when the recommendation is blocked
advanced_layer_requirements: Weight changes require regression fixtures and compatibility review
Expose registry fingerprint and decision receipt for expert audit
Keep assurance and shadow signals non-authoritative

evidence_annotations.reasoning: Automated shared-contract, deterministic engine, hard-eligibility, provenance, anchor, context, registry, receipt, assurance, signal, and intake-audit tests pass in the packaged build; local runtime integration remains not performed.
